components.name: Button
components.description: The default action: outlined in a hairline, brass on hover.

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Text Input

components.name: Navigation

components.html: OverviewGlobe
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; width: 204px; padding: 10px; background: var(--rail); } .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 7px 9px; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--text-dim); font: 400 13.5px var(--sans); text-decoration: none; transition: background .16s var(--ease), color .16s var(--ease); } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: rgba(214, 190, 138, 0.08); color: var(--text); } .ds-nav-item[aria-current='page'] { background: rgba(214, 190, 138, 0.15); color: var(--brass); font-weight: 520; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--brass); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: A hairline strip whose pressed option takes the brass tint.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-seg button { border: 0; background: transparent; padding: 5px 12px; color: var(--text-dim); font: 400 13px var(--sans); cursor: pointer; transition: background .16s var(--ease), color .16s var(--ease); } .ds-seg button[aria-pressed='true'] { background: rgba(214, 190, 138, 0.16); color: var(--brass); } .ds-seg button:hover:not([aria-pressed='true']) { color: var(--text); }

components.name: Card
components.description: A plate-blue surface with a soft hairline and no shadow.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--bg-1); border: 1px solid var(--line-soft); border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; max-width: 320px; } .ds-card-head { padding: 11px 14px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft); } .ds-card-head h2 { font: 560 13.5px/1.25 var(--sans); letter-spacing: -0.012em; color: var(--text); margin: 0; } .ds-card-body { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 10px; padding: 14px; font: 400 12.5px var(--sans); color: var(--text); } .ds-host { font-family: var(--mono); } .ds-num { color: var(--red); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.description: One line through ordered stations in the ink kept for it, with the deciding station marked.
components.html:
1. Client rules

  2. Allow list
    Not listed
  3. Block list

components.css: .ds-trace { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; display: grid; } .ds-stop { position: relative; padding: 0 0 14px 24px; } .ds-stop::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 4px; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--bg-1); border: 2px solid var(--violet); z-index: 1; } .ds-stop::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 5px; top: 14px; bottom: -6px; width: 2px; background: var(--violet); opacity: .55; } .ds-stop:last-child { padding-bottom: 0; } .ds-stop:last-child::after { display: none; } .ds-decided::before { background: var(--red); border-color: var(--red); } .ds-title { font: 520 13.5px var(--sans); color: var(--text); } .ds-decided .ds-title { color: var(--red); } .ds-detail { font: 400 13px/1.5 var(--sans); color: var(--text-dim); }

narrative.overview:
Orbis draws the network as a body with things in orbit around it, the way an observatory draws the sky. The ground is true Prussian blue, structure is engraved in pale brass, and text is ivory. Ink colour carries meaning and is rationed: jade for safe and live, vermilion for a stop, violet for a traced decision.

Density is that of a working instrument. Body type is 14px, cards are compact, and figures use tabular numerals so a column of live values holds still. The first screen of the Overview is one engraved plate rather than a grid of cards. Depth comes from a step of tone and a hairline. Motion is slow and continuous on the chart, quick and settled on controls, and it stops the moment nobody is looking.

The world refuses the category default of near-black panels with a neon accent. It has no glass, no glow and no additive blending.
keyCharacteristics: Prussian ground in four tonal steps, with brass hairlines instead of shadows for structure.
Colour as a rationed ink, each hue holding one job.
One workhorse sans, Geist, with a mono only for strings a machine reads.
A decision is always one line through ordered stations.
Live values change in place and columns never move.
Everything drawn is real data from this network.

rules.name: The Reserved Ink Rule
rules.body: Violet is the traced decision and nothing else. If a surface is not showing how one decision was reached, it contains no violet.

rules.name: The Vermilion Rule
rules.body: Vermilion means a block or a threat, and nothing else. It is never decoration, never a brand accent, and never a chart series for ordinary traffic.

rules.name: The Tinted State Rule
rules.body: A state chip is its ink as text, the same ink at about 8% as fill, and at about 25% as border. Solid fills are kept for the primary action and an armed destructive button.

rules.name: The Machine String Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for addresses, ports, hostnames and config keys, which include rule text, file names and model ids. Counts, rates and byte sizes stay in Geist with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Security Read Rule
rules.body: The block page headline is set in mono because that hostname is a security read: rn and m, l and 1 must stay distinct. This is the one headline in the system that is not Geist.

rules.name: The In-Place Rule
rules.body: Live values change in place. Tabular figures are on globally and columns never move, so a number updating is the only thing that happens.

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: The first screen of the Overview is one engraved surface divided by hairlines, not a grid of cards.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: Controls are at least 44px tall on phones. Buttons, navigation items and segmented controls get this at 880px and below, and block page buttons have it everywhere.

rules.name: The Step and Hairline Rule
rules.body: A surface separates from its parent by one tonal step and a hairline. Cards never carry a shadow.

rules.name: The No Light Rule
rules.body: Nothing emits light. No glass, no backdrop blur, no coloured shadow, no additive blending. All three.js materials use normal blending, and light on the chart is drawn as ink.

rules.name: The Held Fire Rule
rules.body: Destructive buttons stay outlined until hovered or focused. The confirm dialog uses this same button for its confirm action.

rules.name: The One Line Rule
rules.body: A decision is one line through ordered stations, in order, with the deciding station marked. It is never a table of checks or a stack of cards.

rules.name: The Still Sky Rule
rules.body: Motion is transform and opacity on drift, a single pass along a path, and quick settling on state changes. The chart, the globe and the block page all stop their loops when the tab is hidden, and under reduced motion they stop moving and draw still. The orbit chart also pauses when it is scrolled off screen.

dos: Do use the true Prussian ramp, rail #003153, ground #041c2f and plate #06263e, for every surface.
Do rule structure with brass hairlines and separate surfaces with one tonal step.
Do keep jade for safe and live, and vermilion for a stop or a fault.
Do use rose where a category needs a fourth hue. Violet is never the spare.
Do set hostnames, addresses, ports and config keys in Geist Mono, and everything else in Geist.
Do draw any decision as one line through ordered stations with the deciding station marked.
Do update live values in place with tabular figures.
Do treat the shield flare and the plate-coloured halo behind chart lettering as ink. They are strokes, not glow.
Do stop every animation loop when the tab is hidden and draw a still frame under reduced motion.
Do give controls a 44px minimum height on phones.
donts: Don't use violet for anything but a traced decision: not selection, not a chart series, not a badge.
Don't use vermilion for ordinary traffic, decoration or emphasis.
Don't use backdrop blur, glass panels, coloured shadows or additive blending.
Don't put a shadow on a card. Shadows are for things that float.
Don't fill a destructive button at rest.
Don't set counts, rates or byte sizes in mono.
Don't show traffic that is not real, on the chart or the block page.
Don't use a loop that keeps running on a hidden tab. The node is a Raspberry Pi.
Don't let a live update move a column or reflow a row.
